resources.string: Settings saved for new games against the computer.

Chess with Life is an offline app for two players sharing one Android device or for playing against the computer.

Version: 0.2 beta

The built-in game engine is based on Fairy-Stockfish, an open-source engine for chess and chess variants. The project fork is adapted for the Chess with Life rules.

Fairy-Stockfish project: https://github.com/fairy-stockfish/Fairy-Stockfish
Adapted fork: https://github.com/SCP1715/Fairy-Stockfish
Engine license: GNU General Public License version 3 (GPL-3.0); source code and license text are available in the fork repository.

The app works offline. The game does not use network services or accounts.

The goal is to capture every opponent king. Two players share one device; no network or accounts are used.

Players take turns. Pieces follow standard chess geometry and sliding pieces need a clear path. A pawn may advance two squares on its first move, captures diagonally, and promotes on the last rank. En passant is available immediately after a two-square pawn move.

An attacked king does not restrict moves. Players are responsible for their own kings. A king may capture a friendly piece, including another king; the moving king remains on the board. Check is not announced and attacked kings are not highlighted.

If, after a pawn move, at least one king of that side is attacked, promotion to a king becomes available. This creates a debt: the next player must capture any king of that side. The capturing side has no king-safety restriction. If the debt is paid, the game continues, and the capture creates a new king, a counter-debt is created. Capturing the last king ends the game immediately.

Kingside, queenside, and vertical castling are allowed when the king and rook have not moved and the squares between them are empty. Attacked squares are not checked. A promoted rook is considered unmoved until it moves.

A player who begins a turn with no king loses. Threefold repetition and 50 moves without a capture or pawn move allow a draw claim, but do not end the game automatically. An agreed draw ends only after one player offers and the opponent accepts.

If exactly two kings remain, one of each color, and they are not adjacent (including diagonally), the player to move may claim a draw. It is not automatic; any third piece removes this draw condition.

The editor allows unusual positions without automatically arranging or correcting pieces. To start, the side to move must have a king; an active debt must have at least one legal king capture.
